oracle: protoc (libprotoc 34.1, tier A, the format's reference compiler) compiles each file with --include_source_info through calibration/oracles/protoc-descriptors, under the subject's buf module roots and the repository root; definitions are messages (nested ones and proto2 groups; the synthetic map-entry messages are not written), enums, services and rpcs at their source_code_info spans; references are (enclosing message or rpc, type) for every message- or enum-typed field, map value, oneof member and extension field declared in a message, and an rpc's request and response
per-file times exclude the one-time grammar compile (an untimed warm-up extraction precedes timing)
range, not gated for a tool format: every matched definition's end line equals protoc's span end (1,192 of 1,192); every rpc and message carries a Signature

the incumbent's rpc Signature is the request and response type names joined by an arrow, text no source spells; a tags-engine Signature is the definition's own source up to its body (design section 3.3), so the dialect's is the rpc as written (rpc SayHello (HelloRequest) returns (HelloResponse)) and protoextract_test.go's signature case holds for the incumbent only (TestProtobufDialectRPCSignature)

xref_precision and xref_recall of a tags-engine tool format score the file resolver's file-resolved edges (fusion.ResolveFileEdges over the dialect's import strategy, the edges ingest stores) against the oracle's cross_references at file granularity: (file, referring definition, referenced file), the referenced definition's name not compared (LB-F56)
